pr_body:
Some services like DHCHPv4 directly send raw packets to the iface.
This causes issue when the iface does not implement l2, e.g.
because it is a socket offload interface. fix that.

Fixes: #24382
Signed-off-by: Loic Poulain <loic.poulain@linaro.org>

issue_context.title: disco_l475_iot1 not working with samples/net/wifi
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The ST disco_l475_iot1 is not working with samples/net/wifi when enable DHCPv4

**To Reproduce**
Add below config at prj.conf
_CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS=y
CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4=y_

_west build -b disco_l475_iot1 samples/net/wifi
west flash_

**Expected behavior**
board be capable to have console, connect to wifi network and send a ping.

comments: @nandojve is your IP not managed by WiFi driver? I suppose CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4=n should be instead of y.

Hi @nandojve ,
samples/net/wifi is well working (and specially on disco_l475_iot1, that I tested) for what it is intend to do, as said in the README:
'enabling the Wi-Fi shell module'
You cannot just active few switches to have DHCP up and running. Have a look at "\samples\net\dhcpv4_client", you will see that much more switches need to be activated, and that you need to call more code in your application to start DHCP (see main.c).
Also as you are in wifi (instead of ethernet), before starting dhcp, you will need to connect to a specific wifi network, provide password, ...

I'm start to think that board that I received have some defect. On the regular path following all steps on the wifi demo I can connect to network but I can't see any ping return even from my local network. I don't have a default gateway and netmask. When I enabled below flags wrong characters show on the console and I lose control.

`uart:~$ \���񆿆�ο��YjلO}R��B���᭟�o�1߻��ﻏ_y������׾����ϝo��q]��5�N�O������������������O�`

CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS=y
CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4=y

What could I doing here on wifi demo enabling above flags that could create such problem with console?

PS.: Have the option to enable DHCPv4 on WIFI demo could be a good enhancement.
can you ping your board from another station? I tried that although did not tried ping from the board.
you can also try echo_client from zephyr there is already available Digi Servers available for both UDP and TCP.

> What could I doing here on wifi demo enabling above flags that could create such problem with console?

My 1st guess would be that DHCP starts but the board is not connected to a wifi Access Point.

> You cannot just active few switches to have DHCP up and running. Have a look at "\samples\net\dhcpv4_client", you will see that much more switches need to be activated, and that you need to call more code in your application to start DHCP (see main.c).

If one enables the `CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS=y`, then the operations done in `samples/net/dhcpv4_client` are done automatically meaning `net_dhcpv4_start()` is called by the config lib in that case. The DHCPv4 sample is there just to show how one can enable DHCPv4 if the config settings library is not enabled. So for the other network samples, it should be enough to just enable `CONFIG_NET_DHCPV4=y` as the config settings is enabled already for them. If one has an own application, then one might need to call `net_dhcpv4_start()` manually (if the config settings lib is not enabled).

> any idea about wrong characters on shell when enable DHCPv4 option.

I have not seen this kind of garbage output, but I have not used wifi shell much so this could be something related to that shell.

> If one enables the CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS=y, then the operations done in samples/net/dhcpv4_client are done automatically meaning net_dhcpv4_start() is called by the config lib in that case. 

Ok, so dhcp starts whereas there is not connection to wifi AccessPoint. I suspect garbage comes from there. So maybe it is not good to enable  CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS in this case, but rather in the application, establish first the wifi connection to the Access Point and then only start DHCP.

> Ok, so dhcp starts whereas there is not connection to wifi AccessPoint. I suspect garbage comes from there. So maybe it is not good to enable CONFIG_NET_CONFIG_SETTINGS in this case, but rather in the application, establish first the wifi connection to the Access Point and then only start DHCP.

That sounds like a good plan. The net config settings lib tries to wait until there is a connection available, but if it takes long time, then it might timeout etc.
